docs.title: Automatic cut detection for VFX
docs.text:
Cut detection for VFX shot prep

  • Detect

    Drop in a clip and press Enter. CutDetectorPro analyses every frame and draws a spike graph of the changes. Drag the threshold line to decide which spikes count as cuts.

    Detecting cuts

  • Review

    Step through the cuts with the split viewer, and spot missed ones in the contact sheet. Add or delete a cut with one keypress, and your edits survive threshold changes.

    Fix cuts in seconds

  • Export

    Send the finished shot list to editorial, a PDF or Excel report, sub-clips and thumbnails, Flow Production Tracking (ShotGrid) or straight into Hiero.

    Exporting

  • Automatic cut detection

    Two detectors to pick from. Content-aware for regular cuts, adaptive for footage with fast camera moves.

    Detectors

  • A threshold you can drag

    See every frame-to-frame change as a spike. Move the line and the shots table updates instantly.

    Spike graph

  • Find missing cuts by eye

    The contact sheet shows every frame of a shot at once. Spot the missed cut, click it, press C.

    Contact sheet

  • Read the burn-in (OCR)

    Draw a box around a shot name, timecode or note. The text lands in your shots table.

    Text extraction

  • Clean up the text

    Search and replace, or split S01_010 into a sequence column S01 and a shot column 010, so names match your pipeline.

    Text parsing

  • Analyse just a part of a clip

    Set in and out points and skip the rest. Great for long reels and quick threshold tests.

    Sub-range analysis

  • Analyse once, reopen instantly

    Results are remembered per clip. Save a portable .cdui project with all your manual edits.

    Re-using analyses

  • Exports for every destination

    Editorial (otio, edl, aaf, xml, csv), PDF and Excel reports, mp4 sub-clips, jpg thumbnails, or a paste straight into Flow Production Tracking.

    Exporting

  • Works inside Hiero

    Right-click a clip in the bin, or a track item on the timeline, and get soft cuts back without exporting anything.

    Hiero integration

Detect Review Extract text Export

Dual viewer on top, spike graph below, shots table on the right. Every spike above the yellow threshold line becomes a cut, and shows up in the table straight away.

The contact sheet shows all frames of the current shot. Missed a cut? Click the first frame of the new shot and press C.

Hold Ctrl (Cmd on macOS), draw a box around the burn-in and send the text to a column of your choice.

Export only the flagged shots, bundle files per sequence and write several formats in one go.

  • Editorial: otio, edl, aaf, xml, csv
  • Reports: PDF and Excel with thumbnails
  • Media: mp4 sub-clips and jpg thumbnails
  • Clipboard: ready to paste into Flow Production Tracking (ShotGrid)
Which platforms does it run on?

macOS, Windows and Linux. CutDetectorPro is a standalone app, so there's nothing to install: run it from wherever you downloaded it.

Which video formats can it open?

CutDetectorPro reads video through PySceneDetect and OpenCV, so it opens the common formats such as .mov, .mp4, .mkv and .avi. See Import & Sessions.

What does it cost?

CutDetectorPro is currently in beta, and the beta license is free. Join our Discord to get a key. You can also try the app without one: in demo mode everything works except the export features. See Install & Activate for the details.

Do I need to install anything else?

On most systems, no. Tesseract (for text extraction) and ffmpeg (for exporting sub-clips) come with the app. On the few systems they don't, you can install them yourself. Cut detection, review and all other exports never need either.

Do I have to re-analyse a clip every time I open it?

No. The analysis is saved per clip, and CutDetectorPro offers to reuse it next time. If you save a .cdui project it includes the analysis and all of your manual edits, so it opens instantly and you can send it to a colleague.

My clip is really long. Can I analyse just a section?

Yes. Set an in and an out point and only that range is analysed. See Sub-range analysis.

I found a bug, or I'm missing a feature

Tell us on Discord, or use Help → Report Issues... inside the app.

docs.title: Stop cutting up reference clips by hand
docs.text:
CutDetectorPro finds the cuts in your video for you, makes the last few misses easy to fix, reads shot names straight off the burn-in, and hands you a clean shot list.

docs.title: Shot prep shouldn't eat your day
docs.text: You get a string-out for a bid, or an offline edit at turnover, as one long movie file. Somebody now has to find every cut, name every shot and type it all into a spreadsheet. That's hours of scrubbing, and one missed cut can ripple through the whole schedule.

docs.title: Pricing
docs.text:
Pricing

Licenses can be deactivated and reactivated at any time.

  • Detection and review

    Content and adaptive detectors, spike graph, contact sheet, sub-range analysis.

  • Text extraction

    OCR for burn-ins, search & replace, and columns split from other columns.

  • Every export

    otio, edl, aaf, xml, csv, PDF, Excel, mp4 sub-clips, jpg thumbnails and the Flow Production Tracking clipboard.

  • Hiero integration

    Launch from a bin item or the timeline and get soft cuts back.

  • Portable sessions

    Save everything in a .cdui file and reopen it instantly, on any machine.

  • Fast previews

    A frame cache for smooth scrubbing, plus shot playback at the press of the spacebar.

Can I try it first?

Yes. Without a license key CutDetectorPro runs in demo mode: everything works except the export features. Download it and see for yourself.

What is an activation?

An activation ties your license key to one computer. A license with 4 activations can run on 4 computers at the same time.

Can I move my license to a new computer?

Yes. Deactivate the old machine from Help → Deactivate License... and activate the new one.

How does renewal work?

Your license is a yearly subscription, handled by our payment provider Lemon Squeezy, and it renews automatically. About a week before it renews, you get a reminder email.

You can cancel (or resume) any time in the customer portal. If you cancel, your license keeps working until the end of the year you've paid for. After that it expires (see below).

What if a renewal payment fails?

The payment is retried automatically, four times over two weeks. Each time it fails you get an email asking you to update your billing details, and your license keeps working in the meantime.

If the last attempt also fails, the subscription ends and the license expires. An expired license can't be reactivated: all of its activations become invalid and you need to buy a new license.

What happens in the app when my license expires?

CutDetectorPro checks your license online about once a week, so it can take up to a week to notice. Then it tells you that your license has expired and switches to demo mode. Everything except exporting keeps working, and you can buy a new license at any time to unlock exporting again. See Install & Activate.

docs.title: Contact Sheet
docs.text: The contact sheet is the best way to find cuts the detector missed. Click Find Missing Cuts (or press `) and every frame of the current shot is laid out in a grid. A missed cut is easy to spot: the picture suddenly changes.

docs.title: Add a missing cut
docs.text:
1. Look through the frames of the shot for the point where a new shot begins.
  2. Click the first frame of the new shot (or move to it with the arrow keys).
  3. Press C.

That's it. The cut is added to the Shots Table and stays there, even if you change the threshold later.

docs.title: Find your way around
docs.text:
• The Spike Graph zooms in to only show the spikes of the current shot, which helps to spot a missed cut inside it.
  • A small graph map above the main graph shows where the current shot sits within the whole clip.
  • Use the sliders under the sheet to change the brightness and size of the thumbnails. Brighten dark shots, or enlarge the frames to compare details.

Keys for the contact sheet

  • Page Up / Page Down move to the previous or next shot.
  • Left / Right select the previous or next frame.
  • Up / Down select the frame above or below.
  • ` switches back to the graph.

The selected frame has an orange outline.

docs.title: Detecting Cuts
docs.text: Press a button, wait a moment, and every change in the picture shows up as a spike in the Spike Graph.

docs.title: Analyse a clip
docs.text:
Do one of the following:

  • Click Analyse in the lower left corner
  • Press Enter

That's it. CutDetectorPro compares every frame with the one before it and draws the difference as a spike. Then you set the threshold to decide which spikes count as cuts.

docs.title: Pick a detector
docs.text:
There are two ways to analyse a clip. Choose with the Content and Adaptive buttons next to Analyse.

  • Content

    The classic detector. It spots hard cuts by measuring how much two neighbouring frames differ. Anything above your threshold is a cut, and you can move the threshold after the analysis is done.

    Details

  • Adaptive

    Like Content, but it compares each change with a rolling average of the frames around it. Try it when fast camera moves cause false cuts.

    Details

docs.title: Analyse only part of the picture
docs.text:
Got a burn-in that changes with every shot? Analysing just the burn-in is often more accurate than analysing the whole frame.

  1. Hold Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) and drag a rectangle over the region.
  2. A purple outline shows the area. Only that area is analysed.
  3. Right-click to delete the rectangle again.

The rectangle always stays on the picture: if you start dragging outside of the image, it's trimmed to the image edge, and if the drag never reaches the image the rectangle is removed.

This is different from a sub-range

The rectangle limits the analysis to a region of each frame. A sub-range limits it to a span of frames. You can combine both.

docs.title: Re-use a previous analysis
docs.text:
You only ever analyse a clip once. The results are saved automatically, and next time you import the same clip CutDetectorPro offers to load them instead:

Where the saved analyses live

Each clip gets its own csv file:

  • Windows: %APPDATA%\CutDetectorPro\OHUfx (roaming profile)
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/CutDetectorPro/OHUfx
  • Linux: ~/.local/share/CutDetectorPro/OHUfx

You normally never need to look in there.

Sharing your work

Saving a project bundles the analysis data into the .cdui file, so the file is fully portable. See Import & Sessions.

docs.title: Exporting
docs.text:
The Shots Table is your cut list. Exporting turns it into whatever the next person in the chain needs.

Exporting needs an activated license

In demo mode the export features are switched off. See Install & Activate.

docs.title: Two ways to export
docs.text:
• Quick Export

    One click from File → Quick Export. Pick a category and a format and you're done. It always exports all shots, whatever is flagged in the table.

  • Export Manager

    File → Export Manager... for more control. Export several formats in one go, only the flagged shots, and bundle the files by any column.

docs.title: What you can export
docs.text:
• Editorial data

    For importing into editorial applications.

    • otio
    • edl
    • aaf
    • xml
    • csv

  • Reports

    For human eyes and brains: thumbnails plus your columns.

    • PDF
    • Excel (xls)

  • Media

    Always handy in this job.

    • mp4 sub-clips, one per shot
    • jpg thumbnails (1024 px wide)

    Sub-clips use ffmpeg, which comes with the app on most systems

  • Clipboard

    Copies your shots to the clipboard so you can paste them straight into Autodesk Flow Production Tracking (formerly ShotGrid) to create new shots.

docs.title: Export Manager tips
docs.text:
• Flagged Only: tick the Flag checkbox on the shots you want in the table, then choose Flagged Only to export just those.
  • One file per... (editorial): write a separate file per value of any column. For example, one otio per sequence.
  • Bundle by... (media): sort thumbnails and sub-clips into a folder per value of any column, for example one folder per sequence.
  • Several formats at once: tick as many as you like.
  • The manager describes in plain words what it is about to do, so you can check it before you export.

Missing a format?

Tell us on Discord and we'll see what we can do.

docs.title: FAQ & Troubleshooting
docs.text: Quick answers to the things people ask most. Not here? Ask on Discord or use Help → Report Issues... in the app. When you do, please include your support info. See Getting help.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Which platforms does it run on?

macOS, Windows and Linux. CutDetectorPro is a standalone app, so there's nothing to install. See Install & Activate.

macOS says the app bundle is corrupt

That's macOS being cautious about an app that isn't notarised yet. There's a short video on the Install & Activate page that shows how to get past it.

A clip won't open

CutDetectorPro reads video through PySceneDetect and OpenCV, so it opens what those can decode. Transcode the clip to an h264 .mp4 and try again. See Import & Sessions.

docs.title: License
docs.text:
What can I do without a license?

Everything except exporting. In demo mode you can import, detect, review and fix cuts, extract text and play back shots. The export features and Hiero's Apply button need an activated license.

I'm moving to a new computer

Choose Help → Deactivate License... on the old machine, then activate on the new one. See Install & Activate.

My license expired

When a license expires, all of its activations become invalid and a new purchase is required. Until then CutDetectorPro runs in demo mode: exporting is switched off but everything else keeps working. See the pricing page for how renewals and expiry work. Not sure why yours expired? Check the subscription in the customer portal or ask on Discord .

Do I need to be online?

Only now and then. CutDetectorPro re-checks your license about once a week, and keeps working for up to 14 days if you're offline at that point.

docs.title: Cut detection
docs.text:
I get too many cuts
  • Drag the threshold up.
  • Try the Adaptive detector if there is a lot of camera motion.
  • Analyse just the burn-in with the region rectangle.
  • Delete individual false positives in Preview Mode.
I get too few cuts
  • Drag the threshold down.
  • Use the Contact Sheet to find the cuts that are missing and add them with C.
Do I have to analyse a clip every time?

No. The analysis is remembered per clip, and saved inside your .cdui session too. See Re-use a previous analysis.

The clip is long. Can I analyse just a part?

Yes, with a sub-range.

docs.title: Text extraction
docs.text:
Text extraction doesn't work

Text extraction needs Tesseract, which comes with the app on most systems. Open Help → About CutDetectorPro → Environment to see whether CutDetectorPro found one and where it's from. If it can't find one, clicking a column's icon shows a Tesseract not found message. If it didn't (on Intel Macs, older macOS versions and ARM Windows or Linux, for example), install Tesseract yourself, or point Preferences to the executable.

The text has mistakes
  • Draw the rectangle tighter around the text.
  • Fix repeating mistakes (an "S" read as "$", say) with Search & Replace.
  • Text extraction reads English. Text in other languages will come out with mistakes.

docs.title: Exporting
docs.text:
The export options are greyed out

You need an activated license. Sub-clip export also needs ffmpeg, which comes with the app on most systems. Help → About CutDetectorPro → Environment shows whether one was found.

Does sorting the table change the export order?

No. You can sort the Shots Table freely, but exports and saved sessions always use the shots in time order.

How do I export only some of the shots?

Tick the Flag checkbox on those shots, then use the Export Manager with Flagged Only.

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
Scrubbing is slow

Fill the frame cache: hit the ghost and let Pacman finish.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
What should I send when I report a problem?

Use Help → Report Issues... and tick Include log files and system info. The report then carries your recent session logs and a system_info.txt: your app, Python, Qt and system versions, your license status, which ffmpeg and Tesseract are in use (and how they were found), the relevant environment variables and where the log and settings live.

Prefer to ask on Discord ? Open Help → About CutDetectorPro, click Copy Support Info and paste it into your message. It's the same text.

Which open-source software does CutDetectorPro use?

The Credits tab of Help → About CutDetectorPro lists every third-party project with its developers, license and version. The license texts, including those of the bundled ffmpeg and Tesseract, also ship with the app in a licenses folder, and the About dialog links to it.

docs.title: Frame Cache
docs.text: Scrubbing through a video is only smooth if the frames are ready. The frame cache keeps them in memory so the whole UI feels snappy.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Frames are stored at up to 1024 pixels wide, as compressed jpg data, so the memory footprint stays small.
  • One cache is shared by everything that shows frames: the viewers, the Contact Sheet, the Shots Table and the Shot Playback.
  • Anything you do (scrubbing, playing a shot, opening the contact sheet) adds the frames it needs to the cache on demand.

docs.title: Fill it up front
docs.text:
For the smoothest experience, hit the ghost on the cache bar, watch Pacman do his thing, and enjoy a fast UI afterwards.

Cut analysis is not affected by the cache

The cache only speeds up what you see. The detection itself always reads the video directly.

docs.title: Caching a sub-range
docs.text:
If you have requested a sub-range (in and out points), the ghost only caches the frames of that range instead of the whole clip.

Changing the range never switches caching on by itself. But if caching is already on, CutDetectorPro caches any frames of the new range that aren't cached yet.

docs.title: Hiero
docs.text:
Using Foundry's Hiero? Launch CutDetectorPro right from a bin item or a track item and get soft cuts back, with no exporting and importing in between.

Needs an activated license

The Apply button that sends results back to Hiero is one of the features that is switched off in demo mode. See Install & Activate.

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
Hiero needs to know where CutDetectorPro's plugin lives. Pick one of these:

Default plugin folder Environment variable

Create this file:

$HOME/.nuke/Python/StartupUI/load_cutdetector.py

Paste the following into it and save:

import hiero.core
# update the below with the valid path to CutDetectorPro's location
hiero.core.addPluginPath("/path/to/CutDetectorPro/plugins/hiero")

Set HIERO_PLUGIN_PATH to the location of CutDetectorPro's plugin folder:

export HIERO_PLUGIN_PATH=/path/to/CutDetectorPro/plugins/hiero

Already using HIERO_PLUGIN_PATH?

Append to its value instead of overwriting it.

Restart Hiero. You should now see Cut Detector in the context menu of bin items and of track items in the timeline:

docs.title: Use it
docs.text:
Launched this way, CutDetectorPro shows an extra Apply button under the Shots Table:

Click it to send the cuts back to Hiero:

What Hiero does with them depends on where you started.

From a bin item From a track item

Right-click a clip in the bin and choose Cut Detector. When you hit Apply, the plugin builds a new Sequence with soft cuts and adds it to the same bin as the clip:

If the clip has an in and/or out point set in Hiero, CutDetectorPro opens with that range already requested, so only that part is analysed (see Sub-range analysis). Without in/out points the whole clip is analysed.

Right-click a track item in the timeline and choose Cut Detector. The part of the clip the track item uses (its source in and out) is requested for you, so only the footage that is actually in your cut gets analysed.

When you hit Apply, the track item is cut up in place:

  • It's split at every cut, as soft cuts.
  • The pieces are named after their shot names.
  • Shots that start outside the track item's range are ignored.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Several windows at once. You can have multiple CutDetectorPro windows open. Each one sends its results back to the item it was launched from, whichever you apply first.
  • Text goes along. If you extracted text with OCR, the results arrive in Hiero as a CutDetectorPro tag on each shot, in both workflows.
  • Behind the scenes. CutDetectorPro and Hiero talk over a simple inter-process connection. The plugin that ships with CutDetectorPro turns the incoming data into Hiero cuts.

Requires CutDetectorPro 0.5.1 or later

Launching from the timeline, and requesting the range from in/out points, are not available in earlier versions.

docs.title: Import & Sessions
docs.text: Getting a clip into CutDetectorPro takes one drag. Getting it back later takes another.

docs.title: Import a clip
docs.text:
Pick whichever you like best:

  • Drag & drop a video file into an empty window
  • Click Import a Clip on the landing page
  • Choose File → Import Clip... from the menu
  • Press Ctrl+I (Cmd+I on macOS)
Which video formats work?

CutDetectorPro reads video through PySceneDetect and OpenCV, so it opens the formats those can decode. That covers the common containers such as .mov, .mp4, .mkv and .avi. The import dialog doesn't filter by file type, so you can pick any file and see if it opens.

If a clip won't open, transcode it to an h264 .mp4 and try again.

docs.title: Save and reload your work
docs.text:
Everything you do lives in a session: the analysis, your threshold, every manual edit and your text columns. Save it as a .cdui file with Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS).

A session file is fully portable. The analysis data is stored inside it, so it opens instantly on any machine and you can hand it to a colleague.

To load one:

  • Drag & drop a .cdui file into an empty window
  • Click Load a Session File on the landing page
  • Choose File → Load Session... from the menu
  • Press Ctrl+O (Cmd+O on macOS)

You don't have to save just to avoid re-analysing

CutDetectorPro also remembers the analysis of every clip on its own, and offers to reuse it next time you import that clip. See Re-use a previous analysis.

docs.title: What's next?
docs.text:
• Detect cuts

    Press Analyse and let CutDetectorPro do the work.

    Detecting cuts

  • Only part of the clip?

    Set in and out points before you analyse.

    Sub-range analysis

docs.title: Install & Activate
docs.text:
Getting from download to your first cut list takes a few minutes. CutDetectorPro is a standalone app for macOS, Windows and Linux, so there's no installer to run.

flowchart LR
    A[Download] --> B[Launch] --> C[Import a clip] --> D[Activate to export]

docs.title: 1. Download and launch
docs.text:
Download CutDetectorPro from the beta download folder and unpack it wherever you like. It runs right where it is, so there's nothing to install.

macOS: “the app bundle is corrupt” warning

On macOS you may see a warning about a corrupt app bundle the first time you open the app. This is macOS being cautious about an app that isn't yet notarised by Apple. This video shows how to get past it:

Once CutDetectorPro is out of beta I'll pay for Apple's certification, and this warning will go away.

docs.title: 2. Activate your license
docs.text:
You can try CutDetectorPro straight away. Without a license key it runs in demo mode: you can import clips, detect and fix cuts and extract text, but the export features are switched off (and so is the Apply button of the Hiero integration). An orange UNLICENSED bar in the status bar reminds you.

To unlock everything, activate a license key. The beta license is free, so join our Discord to get yours.

  1. Click the orange UNLICENSED bar, or choose Help → Activate License...
  2. Enter your license key in the Activate CutDetectorPro dialog and confirm.
  3. That's it. The key is now tied to this machine, and the exports are enabled.
Moving to a different computer?

Choose Help → Deactivate License... on the old machine to free up the activation, then activate on the new one.

Does it need an internet connection?

Only occasionally. CutDetectorPro re-checks your license online about once a week. If you're offline when that happens, it keeps working for up to 14 days and shows you how many are left.

docs.title: 3. Tesseract and ffmpeg
docs.text:
Two features rely on free third-party tools. Both come with CutDetectorPro on most systems, so you normally don't have to install anything:

Tool Used for Included with the app on Tesseract (English) Text extraction (OCR) from burn-ins macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later), Windows (64-bit), Linux (x86_64) ffmpeg Exporting mp4 sub-clips per shot macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows (64-bit), Linux (x86_64 and ARM)

On any other system, install Tesseract and/or ffmpeg yourself. Without them, everything else still works: text extraction is unavailable and the clip export options are greyed out.

docs.title: Which copy does the app use?
docs.text:
CutDetectorPro looks for each tool in this order, and uses the first one it finds:

  1. The path in the environment variable CDUI_TESSERACT_PATH or CDUI_FFMPEG_PATH
  2. The path you set in Preferences
  3. The copy that ships with the app
  4. One installed on your system (on your PATH, or in the usual install folders)

So if you'd rather use your own build, point Preferences at it and it takes priority over the bundled one. To see exactly which one is in use, open Help → About CutDetectorPro → Environment. It shows the path, how it was found and its version.

docs.title: Tesseract (text extraction)
docs.text:
Tesseract is an open-source tool that reads text from images. You only need to install it yourself on systems where it isn't included, or to use your own copy.

Windows macOS Linux
  1. Download the installer from the UB Mannheim builds, the most widely used Windows distribution.
  2. Run it. The default install location is fine.
  3. Make sure Add to PATH is ticked.
  4. Check it worked by opening a Command Prompt and running:
tesseract --version

The easiest way is Homebrew:

brew install tesseract
tesseract --version

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt update
sudo apt install tesseract-ocr

# Fedora / RHEL
sudo dnf install tesseract

tesseract --version
Which languages can it read?

Text extraction reads English. The Tesseract that ships with the app contains English language data only.

docs.title: ffmpeg (clip export)
docs.text:
ffmpeg is the standard tool for converting and cutting video. CutDetectorPro uses it to write one mp4 sub-clip per shot. You only need to install it yourself on systems where it isn't included, or to use your own copy.

Windows macOS Linux 
winget install Gyan.FFmpeg
ffmpeg -version

Prefer a manual install? Download a build from the ffmpeg download page and add its bin folder to your PATH.

brew install ffmpeg
ffmpeg -version

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt update
sudo apt install ffmpeg

ffmpeg -version

On Fedora and RHEL, ffmpeg is available through RPM Fusion.

docs.title: Text Extraction (OCR)
docs.text:
Burn-ins hold gold: shot names, source timecodes, version numbers, VFX notes. CutDetectorPro can read them for you and put the text in your Shots Table, one row per shot. Then you can clean it up until it matches your pipeline's naming.

Powered by Tesseract

Text extraction uses the free Tesseract engine, which comes with CutDetectorPro on most systems. It reads English text. On other systems, install Tesseract and CutDetectorPro finds it automatically.

docs.title: Extract text from the image
docs.text:
1. Switch to Preview Mode (click Check Cut Points).
  2. Hold Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) and drag a rectangle around the text you want, for example part of a burn-in.
  3. Click the icon in the header of the column that should receive the text.

CutDetectorPro reads that area for every shot and fills the column.

Don't have a column yet? Add one first.

The rectangle stays on the picture

If you start dragging outside of the image, the rectangle is trimmed to the image edge. If the drag never reaches the image, the rectangle is removed again.

What if it says \"Tesseract not found\"?

Clicking the icon shows a Tesseract not found message when CutDetectorPro can't find Tesseract. Install it and select it in Preferences, or set CDUI_TESSERACT_PATH. See Install & Activate. If a cell shows [ERROR: tesseract not found] or [ERROR: tesseract failed] instead of text, the same applies.

docs.title: Clean up the text
docs.text: OCR isn't perfect. In the recording above, for example, an "S" sometimes came through as a "$". You have two tools to fix that and to reshape the results.

docs.title: Search & replace
docs.text: Right-click a column header and choose Search&Replace.

docs.title: Split a column into new ones
docs.text:
Say your "Shot Name" column holds values like S01_010, and you also want a "Sequence" column with just S01. Right-click the Shot Name header and choose Extract Additional Column. The new column needs a unique name.

Pick your preview

The dialog previews the value of the row that is selected in the table, so select a representative row first.

There are two ways to pick the part you want:

Tokens Substring

CutDetectorPro splits the text at these characters: _ (underscore), . (period), - (hyphen) and a space. Every part becomes a button. Click the part you want, and a prompt asks for the new column's name.

Prefer to pick by letter position? Switch to Use Substring and select the letters that hold what you need. Click Confirm substring selection and name the new column.

docs.title: Shot Playback
docs.text:
Want to see how a shot actually plays? Press Space and a small player opens right over the window and plays the shot that is selected in the Shots Table, at the source media's frame rate.

Before you have analysed the clip, Space plays the whole clip from the start.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Key What it does Space Open the player Right Step forward one frame Left Step back one frame Up Jump to the first frame Down Jump to the last frame Esc Close the player

The first run can be choppy

The player uses the frame cache. If the shot isn't cached yet, the first playback may be slower than real time. After one run through, it plays smoothly. Fill the cache up front and it's smooth from the start.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
From a movie file to a checked cut list in seven steps. Grab a clip and follow along.

Before you start

Install & activate CutDetectorPro first. You can follow steps 1 to 6 without a license key, but exporting (step 7) needs one.

docs.title: 1. Import a clip
docs.text: Drag a video file into the window, or click Import a Clip on the landing page. (More ways to import are listed in Importing.)

docs.title: 2. Detect cuts
docs.text:
Click Analyse in the lower left corner, or just press Enter. CutDetectorPro looks at every frame and draws a spike wherever the picture changes.

Only need part of the clip?

Press I and O before analysing to set an in and an out point. Only that sub-range is analysed, which is faster for long clips.

More about the two detectors in Detecting Cuts.

docs.title: 3. Set the threshold
docs.text: Every spike that crosses the yellow threshold line becomes a cut and is added to the Shots Table. Drag the line up and down until the cut count looks right. You can change it again at any time.

docs.title: 4. Check the cut points
docs.text:
Press Page Down to jump from cut to cut. The left viewer shows the frame before the cut and the right one the frame at the cut, so they should show two different shots.

If they look the same, it was a false positive. Press Del or Backspace to remove it.

docs.title: 5. Find the missing cuts
docs.text:
Click Find Missing Cuts (or press `) to switch to the Contact Sheet. It shows every frame of the current shot, so a missed cut is easy to spot.

Click the first frame of the new shot and press C to cut. Use the sliders to change the thumbnail size and brightness.

docs.title: 6. Extract text (optional)
docs.text:
Got a burn-in with shot names, timecodes or notes? In Preview Mode, hold Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) and drag a box around the text. Then click the icon in the header of the Shots Table column that should receive it.

Tesseract, the text engine, comes with the app on most systems. See Text Extraction for the details.

docs.title: 7. Export
docs.text:
Open the File menu and choose a Quick Export, or open the Export Manager to write several formats at once. See Exporting for all the options.

Press Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS) to save a .cdui project with your analysis and every manual edit.

docs.title: The two modes in a nutshell
docs.text:
• Preview Mode

    Best for checking the cuts you have. Jump between them with Page Up and Page Down and make sure the two viewers show different shots.

  • Contact Sheet Mode

    Best for finding the cuts you missed. Scan all frames of a shot, pick the first frame of the new one and press C.

Both modes are the recommended way to edit results, because you see exactly where each cut happens. You can also select spikes in the Spike Graph and add or remove them, but the frames aren't visible in that workflow.

docs.title: v0.5.1 (beta)
docs.text:
Hiero: CutDetectorPro can now be launched from a track item in the timeline. The range used by the track item is analysed and the track item is cut up in place. See Hiero

Hiero: when launched from a bin item, the clip's in/out points are used as a sub-range

ffmpeg now ships with the app (a GPL build with libx264), so exporting sub-clips works without installing anything. See Install & Activate

Tesseract (with English language data) now ships with the app on macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 15+), Windows (64-bit) and Linux (x86_64), so text extraction works without installing anything. Other systems keep using an installed Tesseract

New Help → About CutDetectorPro dialog: license status, credits, which ffmpeg and Tesseract are in use (path, how they were found, version), system info and a Copy Support Info button for bug reports

The Shots Table can now be sorted by clicking a column header: ascending, descending, then back to time order. Exports and saved sessions always stay in time order. See Shots Table

The app looks for ffmpeg and Tesseract in this order: environment variable, Preferences, the copy that ships with the app, then your system

Exporting sub-clips now uses exactly the ffmpeg CutDetectorPro found (previously it could pick up a different one on your PATH)

The license texts of the app and of the bundled third-party software now ship with the app in a licenses folder, linked from the About dialog

Column names in the Shots Table must now be unique (ignoring case, also against the built-in columns). CutDetectorPro explains why when a name is refused, and the + button suggests a free one

Caching now respects the requested sub-range. Changing the range no longer starts caching by itself, but new frames of the range get cached if caching is already on

docs.title: Review & Fix Cuts
docs.text:
The automatic detection gets you most of the way. This is where you make sure the cut list is right.

Two questions matter, and CutDetectorPro has a mode for each:

  • Are my cuts real?

    Preview Mode shows the frame before and the frame at each cut, side by side.

    Button: Check Cut Points

  • Did I miss any?

    Contact Sheet Mode shows every frame of a shot at once, so a missed cut jumps out.

    Button: Find Missing Cuts

Switch between the two with the buttons above the graph, or press ` (the backtick key).

docs.title: Preview Mode: check the cuts you have
docs.text:
The right viewer shows the current frame, the one under the playhead in the Spike Graph. The left viewer shows the frame before it. The frame number is also listed in the "Start Frame" column of the Shots Table.

  1. Press Page Down to jump to the next cut. (Page Up goes back.)
  2. Look at the two viewers. They should show two different shots.
  3. If they look the same, it's a false positive. Press Del or Backspace to remove it.

Removed cuts are remembered (they are blacklisted), so moving the threshold later won't bring them back.

docs.title: Contact Sheet Mode: find the cuts you missed
docs.text:
All frames of the current shot are laid out on a sheet, so it's easy to see where a new shot begins. Click the first frame of the new shot (or move to it with the arrow keys) and press C to add the cut.

Full details are on the Contact Sheet page.

docs.title: Fix things by hand
docs.text:
You can also edit straight in the graph, or use the context menu:

Action Shortcut Paint-select spikes in the graph Alt + click & drag Add the selected spikes as cuts A Add a cut at the current frame C Delete the selected spikes D Delete the cut at the current frame Del / Backspace

Your edits stick

Cuts you add are whitelisted and cuts you delete are blacklisted. They stay that way even if you move the threshold afterwards. Added cuts are green in the Shots Table and the graph, deleted ones are red in the graph.

docs.title: Which one should I use?
docs.text:
Both modes are the recommended way to edit, because you see exactly which frame you're cutting on. You can also select spikes in the graph and add or remove them, but in that workflow the frames themselves aren't visible.

All about the spike graph All about the contact sheet

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text: Every keyboard shortcut in one place. On macOS, read Ctrl as Cmd.

docs.title: Anywhere
docs.text: Shortcut Function Ctrl+I Import a clip Ctrl+O Open a session file (.cdui) Ctrl+S Save the session file Ctrl+Q Quit Space Open the Shot Playback ` (backtick) Toggle between the graph and the Contact Sheet (after analysis)

docs.title: Before analysis
docs.text: Shortcut Function Enter Analyse the clip I Set the sub-range in point to the current frame O Set the sub-range out point to the current frame Ctrl + click & drag Draw a rectangle to analyse only that region of the picture

docs.title: Moving through the shots
docs.text:
Shortcut Function Page Down / Down Select the next shot (table row). Does nothing on the last shot. Page Up / Up Select the previous shot. Does nothing on the first shot. Alt + click a table row Jump to that frame and switch to the contact sheet

These keys follow the clip's time order, even while the Shots Table is sorted by another column.

docs.title: Preview Mode
docs.text: Shortcut Function Left / Right Move the playhead one frame back / forward (stays inside the analysed sub-range) Ctrl + click & drag Draw a rectangle for text extraction

docs.title: Contact Sheet
docs.text: Shortcut Function Left / Right Select the previous / next frame Up / Down Select the frame above / below C Cut: add a cut at the selected frame Del / Backspace Delete the cut at the selected frame

docs.title: Spike Graph
docs.text: Shortcut Function C Cut: add a cut at the current frame Del / Backspace Delete the cut at the current frame Alt + click & drag Paint-select spikes A Add the selected spikes as cuts D Delete the selected spikes, so they are never treated as cuts Esc Clear the spike selection

docs.title: Shot Playback
docs.text: Shortcut Function Right / Left Step forward / back one frame Up / Down Jump to the first / last frame Esc Close the player

docs.title: Shots Table
docs.text: The Shots Table is your result: what you see here is what gets exported. So the goal of everything else is to make this table exactly what your workflow needs.

docs.title: Where the rows come from
docs.text:
Every row is a spike in the Spike Graph that is above the threshold, plus every cut you added by hand.

  • Delete a shot by selecting the row and pressing Del or Backspace. The frame is blacklisted, so it stays gone if the threshold changes. Blacklisted frames are drawn red in the graph.
  • Added cuts (whitelisted frames) always get a row, whatever the threshold. They are highlighted in green with a icon, and drawn as green spikes in the graph.

See Review & Fix Cuts for how to add and remove cuts.

Tear it off

The Shots Table can be torn off from the main window and used as a floating panel.

docs.title: The default columns
docs.text:
Column What it holds Start Frame The first frame of the shot Timecode The timecode of that frame. You can set a start timecode above the table to change it. Duration The length of the shot in frames Flag A checkbox for picking specific shots to export. See Exporting. Click the column header to toggle all flags at once.

Columns after those hold text. They are marked with a icon when they can receive text from the text recognition, and you can also edit them by hand.

docs.title: Sort the table
docs.text:
Want the longest shots first, or the shots in name order? Click a column header.

  • First click: sorts ascending. A small arrow on the header shows the sort.
  • Second click: sorts descending.
  • Third click: back to the original order, which is the order the shots appear in the clip.

If the table is already in ascending order (for example when you click Start Frame on a fresh table), the first click goes straight to descending, so a click always changes something you can see.

  • Numbers sort as numbers (Start Frame, Timecode and Duration), and text sorts in natural order without caring about case, so shot_2 comes before shot_10.
  • The Thumbnail header doesn't sort, and the Flag header still toggles the flags.
  • The sort stays as you add, delete or edit shots, and the table scrolls to keep the current shot in view.

Sorting only changes what you see

Exports, saved sessions and text extraction always use the shots in time order, whichever way the table is sorted. The keys that jump to the previous and next cut (Page Up / Page Down and Up / Down) also follow the clip's time order.

docs.title: Add your own columns
docs.text:
Click the button in the upper right corner of the table to add a column with a name of your choice, such as "VFX Notes".

Custom columns can receive OCR text or hold the result of splitting another column, for example to pull a sequence name out of a shot name.

Right-click a custom column's header to rename it (Rename Column...) or remove it (Delete).

Column names have to be unique

A column name can't be empty, and it can't match another column, ignoring upper and lower case and spaces around it. That includes the built-in columns, so you can't add a second "Duration". If a name is taken, CutDetectorPro tells you why and asks again. The button suggests a free name for you (for example "notes 2"). Names identify the columns in your exports and saved sessions, which is why they can't repeat.

docs.title: Next: get text into the table
docs.text:
• Text extraction (OCR)

    Read shot names, timecodes and notes straight off the burn-in.

    Text extraction

  • Export

    Send the table to editorial, reports, media or your tracker.

    Exporting

docs.title: Reading the graph
docs.text:
Once the analysis is done, every frame of the clip is a spike. The taller the spike, the more that frame differs from the one before it. Tall spikes are usually cuts.

  • Click anywhere in the graph to move the playhead. The frame under it shows in the right viewer, the previous frame in the left one.
  • The Shots Table follows the playhead: it always selects the shot the playhead is on.
  • Cuts are drawn in teal, manual additions in bright green and manual deletions in red.

Keys for moving around

  • Left / Right move the playhead one frame at a time (Preview Mode only). After analysis they stay inside the analysed sub-range.
  • Page Up / Page Down and Up / Down jump between cuts (table rows). On the first or last shot nothing happens.
  • Alt + click & drag paint-selects spikes for editing.

All of them are also on the Shortcuts page.

docs.title: The threshold
docs.text: The yellow threshold line decides which spikes count as cuts. Every spike above it turns teal and gets a row in the Shots Table. Drag the line up and down until the number of cuts looks right. Nothing is lost when you move it, and your manual edits are kept.

docs.title: Editing in the graph
docs.text:
Adding cuts Removing cuts

Added cuts are whitelisted: they stay cuts no matter where the threshold is. They're drawn as bright green spikes.

  • Click the spike where the new shot starts (use the arrow keys to step frame by frame), then press C (as in Cut).
  • Or hold Alt and click & drag over one or more spikes, then press A (as in Add).

Removed cuts are blacklisted: they never come back, whatever you do with the threshold. They're drawn as bright red spikes.

  • Move to the cut you don't want (use Page Up / Page Down to go from cut to cut), then press Del or Backspace.
  • Or hold Alt and click & drag over one or more spikes, then press D (as in Delete).

Missing a cut?

The best way to find and add missing cuts is the Contact Sheet: click Find Missing Cuts or press `. You see the actual frames, not just spikes.

docs.title: Analysing a Sub-Range
docs.text:
By default CutDetectorPro analyses the whole clip. But maybe you only care about one section of a long dailies reel, or you want a quick turnaround while testing detector settings. Set an in and an out point, and only that span of frames is analysed.

This is different from the crop region

The rectangle you can draw over the image (see Detecting Cuts) limits the analysis spatially, to a region of each frame such as a burn-in. A sub-range limits it in time, to a span of frames. You can combine the two.

docs.title: Set the range
docs.text:
Set the range before you analyse, in whichever way suits you:

Cache bar handles Hotkeys Command line

Once a clip is loaded, the frame cache bar shows the requested range as a translucent block with two draggable handles: one for the in point, one for the out point.

Drag either handle to adjust the range. By default the range covers the whole clip, so the handles sit at either end until you move them.

With a frame shown in the preview (before analysis), press:

Shortcut Function I Set the requested in point to the current frame O Set the requested out point to the current frame

If a new in point would land past the current out point (or the other way round), the other point snaps to one frame beyond it, so the range never inverts.

When you launch CutDetectorPro from the command line, or from another app such as Hiero, pass:

detect_cuts clip.mov --start-frame 100 --end-frame 400

Frame numbers are 1-based, matching the numbers shown on screen. Leave out either flag to default to the start or end of the clip.

When you launch from Hiero, these are set for you: from the timeline the range is the track item's source range, and from the bin it is the clip's in/out points (if any are set).

Before analysis you can scrub the whole clip to find your in and out points, and the preview starts at the in point.

docs.title: Analyse the range
docs.text:
Click Analyse and only the frames between your in and out points are checked. The rest of the clip is skipped, which is faster on long media.

The Spike Graph and Shots Table only show data for the analysed range, and the last shot's duration ends at the range's out point rather than running to the end of the clip. The first shot of the range is selected when the analysis completes.

After analysis, the Left and Right keys (and the Page Up / Page Down and Up / Down shot navigation) stay inside the analysed range, so the playhead can't wander out of it. The cache bar also zooms in to show just the analysed range, and its handles disappear, because there's nothing else left to select.

Re-using a previous analysis

The saved analysis is named after the requested range, so it's only offered for reuse when the range matches exactly (see Detecting Cuts). Analysing a different range always runs a fresh detection. A full-clip analysis keeps the original filename, so older saved analyses still work.

docs.title: Local frame numbers
docs.text: Once a range has been analysed, the preview shows a shot-relative frame number in brackets next to the global one, for example 142 (12). That is frame 142 of the clip, and the 12th frame of its shot. Handy for judging where you are in a shot without doing the maths.

docs.title: Saving and loading
docs.text: The requested range is stored in your .cdui project. Reopening it restores the same range, re-caches it and zooms the cache bar to it.
